title: HP Account Intelligence — File to JSON Map
purpose: One entry per uploadable file. For each file: what you upload, which JSON it produces, where that JSON is stored and read, and which product features depend on it. Read this alongside hp-input-contract.json, which holds the column-level detail.

how_to_read_an_entry.file_you_upload: The filename and dataset_key you send to the upload API.
how_to_read_an_entry.produces_json: The widget JSON documents this file creates or contributes to. Each is one document in the account_widgets collection.
how_to_read_an_entry.read_by: The API endpoint the frontend calls to get it.
how_to_read_an_entry.supports_features: The product features that stop working, or degrade, without this file.
how_to_read_an_entry.if_missing: What the user actually sees when this file is absent or unreadable.

verified_against: ingestion source code and the reference account files

quick_reference.note: Files ranked by how much of the product depends on them. Send the top of this list first.

table.priority: required for Intent — the primary intent signal
feeds the search index, not a widget

files.format: CSV, one header row, ONE data row (row 0 only)
files.what_it_is: The account's identity card: name, domain, description, industry, location, size and revenue bands.
files.role: THE ANCHOR FILE. It supplies the account domain that every other file is matched against.

example_json.business_description: PT Astra International Tbk is a diversified conglomerate...
example_json.industry_classification: automation machinery manufacturing / Other Industrial Machinery Manufacturing

produces_json.note: Both are BANDS passed through as strings, never parsed as numbers. 'N/A' when blank.

files.stored_in: MongoDB collection account_widgets, one document per widget_key
files.if_missing: Nine of eleven features produce nothing. The Executive Dashboard shows an empty summary card and empty metrics. Worse, without Company Domain the intent features cannot match this account at all, so Intent & Demand Signals reports 'no matched signal' even when the intent files are perfect.
files.most_important_column: Company Domain — it is the join key for the entire system.

files.format: CSV, one header row, ONE data row (row 0 only)
files.what_it_is: The technology stack installed at the account, as one full list plus 20 category columns.

produces_json.note: The category_matrix keys are your EXACT column names, so casing matters: 'It Security', not 'IT Security'.
Maps your stack onto 7 fixed HP categories, marking each as compete, complement or whitespace.

produces_json.contributes: technologies that CONFIRM an intent signal

files.if_missing: The Technographic Map is empty. Intent loses its confirmation layer — an intent signal can no longer be shown as backed by technology the account actually runs, which is what makes it credible.
files.known_problem: 9 cells currently end in '(+11 more)', '(+15 more)' etc. Nothing strips these, so '(+15 more)' appears on screen as if it were a product name. Please export full lists.

files.format: CSV, one header row, one row per contact
files.what_it_is: The people at the account — names, titles, departments, seniority, contact details.
files.important: Column names use the 'Prospect ' prefix with a space: 'Prospect full_name', 'Prospect job_title'. Our older internal doc listed 'Full Name' and 'Title'; those columns do not exist and are not read.

produces_json.note: No contact is ever dropped. Each is scored 0-100 and needs 60+ to be a priority contact.
Department groups, buying-group coverage and a ranked entry path. Computed from the contacts grid — no extra column needed.

files.if_missing: No Stakeholder Map. Content Studio and Message Evaluator have no persona to write for or evaluate against.
watch_out_for: A missing email, phone or LinkedIn lowers the data-completeness score, which can push a real decision maker below the 60-point priority threshold and off the list.
Prospect job_level_main and Prospect job_department_main are controlled vocabularies. A value outside the list still displays but stops matching HP relevance rules.
Supply Prospect prospect_id, or contact IDs are positional and change between refreshes.
Export phone as TEXT. An Excel round-trip turns it into a float with a trailing .0.

files.format: CSV, one header row, one row per topic (149 in the reference file)
files.what_it_is: Bombora Company Surge topic scores — what the account has been researching.
files.note: No domain column; the whole file belongs to one account.

also_needs: intent_topics.csv — for the domain match and the observation date

derived_on_top_of_your_data.intensity: High at 85+, Moderate at 70+, else Low
derived_on_top_of_your_data.theme / hp_category / mapping_status: your topic text matched against the HP topic dictionary
derived_on_top_of_your_data.hiring_linked: true when the topic text contains a staffing term

produces_json.contributes: your topics become the SUPPORTING signals under each HP category

files.if_missing: The intent topic table is empty and every HP category loses its supporting evidence, leaving only the raw category score with nothing behind it.
watch_out_for: Keep the 'family: detail' topic convention — the prefix before the colon drives grouping.
A non-numeric score is NOT treated as zero. The topic is kept, marked excluded, and contributes nothing.
Duplicate topics: the first row wins and the repeat is discarded, never averaged. De-duplicate before sending.

files.format: CSV or Excel, MULTI-FILE — several can coexist
files.what_it_is: News events about the account. This is the PRIMARY news source; news_events.csv is the add-on.

also_needs: news_events.csv — merged into the same feed

signals.headline: Astra Financial Report for the Third Quarter of 2025

produces_json.read_this_to_diagnose_your_delivery: gate_rejection_summary names exactly why rows were dropped. 'older than 365 days' means the delivery was mostly outside the window; 'unparseable date' means a date-format problem. You do not need to ask us.

produces_json.note: the LLM dimension scores behind each signal's tier

files.if_missing: No news feed, and the Executive Dashboard's signal count shows a dash.
watch_out_for: Anything older than 365 days is DISCARDED after a successful upload. A historical back-fill would be thrown away — confirm the window with us first.
Dates must be ISO-8601. '03/04/2025' is read as 4 March, not 3 April.
At most 20 signals are published per account.
Near-identical headlines from different publishers are merged at 85% similarity. That is expected, not a bug.
event_type currently mixes 'launch' with 'M&A'. Pick one casing convention.

files.what_it_is: Structured news events with a category verb and a confidence score. The add-on to google_news.

produces_json.note: Merged into the same feed as google_news. Rows from this file carry location, product and amount; google_news rows do not.

files.if_missing: The news feed still works from google_news alone, but loses the structured event categories (partners_with, acquires, launches) and the location/product/amount detail.
watch_out_for: This file has NO url column, and we will never invent one, so its signals are unlinkable on screen. Only google_news supplies a clickable link.
confidence here is a 0-1 float while google_news uses High/Medium/Low text. Both land in the same field — see open question 5.2.
'identified_as_competitor_of' is treated as a news relationship, not a buying signal, and cannot become a primary signal.
The same 365-day window applies.

files.format: CSV, one header row, one row per posting
files.what_it_is: Open roles at the account, used as a hiring-velocity and urgency proxy.

produces_json.warning: open_job_count counts EVERY row and ignores the status column. The name overstates it — see intent_hiring_demand.open_postings for the filtered figure.

files.if_missing: No hiring-velocity signal on the Executive Dashboard and no Source B demand signal under Intent.
files.biggest_open_question: status is blank on 40% of rows, and blank currently counts as OPEN. That number drives hiring velocity and urgency. Please confirm whether blank means open (emit 'open' explicitly) or unknown (we must stop counting it). This is open question 5.1.
watch_out_for: first_seen_at and last_seen_at are sorted as TEXT. A non-ISO format silently produces wrong first/last dates.
categories must be a valid JSON array. A comma-joined string becomes one bogus category.

files.format: CSV, one header row, ONE data row (row 0 only)
files.what_it_is: Technology detected on the account's public website, plus site-level counts and spend.

produces_json.note: premium_tech_count and web_spend_estimate are RAW STRINGS with no currency or unit attached.

produces_json.contributes: website technologies that confirm an intent signal

files.if_missing: The webstack panel is empty and intent confirmation loses its website-technology evidence.
files.open_question: Cms, Ssl, Web Server, Hosting, Cdn, Framework and Analytics are documented against this file but absent from the delivered version. Which file carries them? (Open question 5.6)

files.format: CSV, one header row, ONE data row (row 0 only)
files.what_it_is: The account's position in its corporate group — parent and ultimate parent.

produces_json.note: Contributes two fields to a card that firmographics.csv mostly builds.

files.if_missing: The parent and ultimate-parent lines on the summary card are blank. Nothing else breaks — but note the Executive Dashboard declares this file as a hard dependency, so if it is registered and then goes missing from the server, the WHOLE feature stops rebuilding.
files.note: An empty Parent Company Name means the company is its own parent. That is valid, not missing data.

files.format: CSV, one header row, one row per detection
files.what_it_is: Individual technology detection events with a confidence score and a first/last-seen window.

produces_json.note: Every value is a STRING, including score. department_onet_codes stays an unparsed JSON string.

files.if_missing: The detections reference panel is empty.
files.known_problem: This file has NO technology or vendor name column, so each row is a score and a date with nothing attached — a detection cannot be labelled on screen. Our older doc claimed a 'vendor' column; it does not exist. Please add the technology name, or confirm the dataset is reference-only. (Open question 5.5)
files.watch_out_for: score here is 0-1, while every other score in the system is 0-100.

files.what_it_is: The metadata row for the intent export — which company it covers, and when it was observed.
files.role: Small file, outsized importance. It is what attaches the intent scores to this account.

produces_json.contributes: the account match, the observation window, and the level-of-intent label

files.if_missing: Intent reports 'unverified' — the scores cannot be tied to this account.
files.most_important_column: Company Website. If it does not normalize-match firmographics.Company Domain, EVERY Bombora topic is discarded and the widget says 'No matched signal' — even when intent_score.csv is perfect. This is the single most load-bearing column in the whole contract.
watch_out_for: Date Stamp is YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20260830.
Send ONE run per file. More than one distinct Date Stamp and no time window is shown at all.
Level Of Intent is empty throughout the current file and is a required input. We need the values and the allowed value set. (Open question 5.4)

files.format: CSV with TWO header rows, wide layout — the only file that breaks the one-header-row rule
files.what_it_is: Per-HP-category intent scores: PCs, Workstations, Poly, Printers, 3D Printers.
files.role: THE PRIMARY INTENT SIGNAL. Everything else in the intent feature supports the numbers in this file.

layout.row_1: category group names, each above the 10 columns it spans
layout.row_2: field names, repeated per category block
layout.row_3_onward: one row per company per run

built_from_your_columns: and all 10 fields per category block

files.if_missing: The HP category cards have no primary score. The feature falls back to Bombora topics only, which support a category but never establish one.
watch_out_for: Domain must normalize-match firmographics.Company Domain, or the WHOLE file is ignored for this account.

Intent Trend is NOT drawn as a trend. With one run and no prior score there is nothing to verify it against, so it is kept as the file's own words. Supplying a prior-window score would let it become a real trend.
Top HP Category is re-checked, not trusted. We recompute the highest-scoring category and show whether your stated top matches.
The terms 'sla' and 'identified as competitor of' are flagged as noisy and bar a category from becoming the account's primary one.
Several runs per domain is fine — the greatest Run Date wins. Keep it ISO so it sorts correctly.

files.file_you_upload: any PDF — annual report, exchange filing, monthly market report
files.format: PDF only, MULTI-FILE — a filing history is several documents
files.what_it_is: The account's filed documents. THE ONLY source of a reported financial figure — every other file carries a band or a category.

produces_json.json_document: NONE — this file does not produce a widget
produces_json.instead: It is parsed into the retrieval corpus (a searchable, citable evidence index), not into an account_widgets document.
produces_json.stored_in: the shared vector index, with page-level citations
produces_json.used_for: Grounded answers and reported financial figures on the Executive Dashboard, where a claim can be traced to a page number.

files.stored_in: Retrieval/vector index (not account_widgets). Index updates are QUEUED after upload, never run inline, because a build takes minutes.
files.read_by: The Executive Dashboard corpus and grounded-answer paths
supports_features: Executive Dashboard — reported financial figures with citations
files.if_missing: No reported financial figure exists anywhere in the product. Revenue is only ever the band from firmographics.csv.
watch_out_for: A REAL TEXT LAYER IS REQUIRED. Pages are parsed from word coordinates, so a scanned or photocopied page is dropped entirely. Send digitally generated PDFs.
A figure is only usable when metric + period + value + unit are all recoverable from the SAME page.

The unit must be printed on the page — a scale word (billion / miliar / juta) and a currency (IDR / Rp / USD) within 60 characters of each other. A page stating no unit yields ZERO figures, by design, because an unlabelled number cannot be cited. Keep the 'expressed in billions of Rupiah' sentence on EVERY page of tables, not just the first.
Figures bind by POSITION. The count of figures in a row must match the number of period columns, so merged cells or a footnote marker glued to a number unbinds the whole row.
Indonesian and bilingual passages are indexed but never made citable. English narrative is what becomes quotable.

files_you_can_upload_but_that_do_nothing.warning: These 12 dataset_keys are accepted by the API and return HTTP 201, but NO code reads a single column from any of them. Uploading produces no JSON, no widget, and no change on screen.
files_you_can_upload_but_that_do_nothing.how_to_confirm: The upload response's `regenerated` array comes back EMPTY for these keys.

keys.note: deliberately excluded — holds role shares, not technologies
not consumed under this key; a file filed as category 'news_events' IS picked up

files_you_can_upload_but_that_do_nothing.action: Tell us which of these you actually intend to deliver. We will either build consumers or close the keys so an upload cannot silently do nothing. (Open question 5.8)

features_and_the_files_they_need.note: The reverse view. A feature produces NOTHING AT ALL if any file listed here is registered but unreadable — stored widgets are left untouched rather than overwritten with empty data.

how_to_check_your_upload_worked.why_this_matters: Nothing validates your column names. A file with entirely wrong headers returns HTTP 201 Created and then produces empty widgets with no error anywhere. The upload response is your only feedback channel.

checks.bad_sign: 0 or 1 on a file you expect to be large
checks.means: the parse found no rows — check delimiter and quoting
no feature consumed this file. Expected only for the 12 unconsumed keys
the file stored but a feature could not rebuild. Previous widgets were left intact, not wiped

step_2_fetch_the_widget.check: status should be 'available'. 'empty' means the file produced no usable rows. 'pending' means an LLM widget has no API key configured — not a data problem.

how_to_check_your_upload_worked.step_3_for_news_read_the_funnel: news_signals_feed publishes raw_signal_count, gate_rejected_count and gate_rejection_summary, which names exactly why rows were dropped.

the_six_things_that_fail_silently.cause: A header name differs in case or has trailing whitespace
the_six_things_that_fail_silently.effect: That column reads as blank; the widget shows N/A

the_six_things_that_fail_silently.cause: firmographics.Company Domain missing or not normalized
hp_category_intent has no row matching the domain
the_six_things_that_fail_silently.effect: ALL HP category scores discarded — the primary intent signal

the_six_things_that_fail_silently.cause: Non-ISO dates in job_openings first_seen_at / last_seen_at

the_six_things_that_fail_silently.effect: Wrong dates, and the 365-day gate then drops the signal

the_six_things_that_fail_silently.summary: Failures 2, 3 and 4 are all ONE root cause — domain normalization — and together they account for the entire intent feature. If you check one thing, check that firmographics.Company Domain, intent_topics.Company Website and hp_category_intent.Domain all resolve to the identical bare host.
